title: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
lede: A GPU Partner tutorial walks Windows users through running Qwen or Inkling 2 Mini locally in Unsloth Desktop, then sharing the model with everyone on a home network.

points: The recipe: install Unsloth Desktop, download a quantized model sized to the GPU's VRAM, set the context length, and turn on LAN access.
The author runs Qwen3.8-27B at 4-bit (UD-Q4_K_XL) with a 128K context on a 32GB RTX 5090.
A table maps VRAM tiers from 8GB to 32GB+ to suggested models, quants and context sizes, with MoE models spilling into system RAM.
Inkling 2 Mini fits the same 32GB card; Inkling 2 Small, at 594B parameters, needs a large unified-memory machine.

points.text: Even enthusiasts concede that, for now, a subscription is the practical route unless privacy or a narrow use case demands local.
Many share cheaper rigs than an RTX 5090, such as a used workstation with a Tesla P100 for under $1k running a capable model at 30 tok/s.
Some skip guides entirely and have a coding agent choose, install and benchmark local models for their hardware.
Commenters reject the claim that you need a Windows PC with a GPU, and a reply reads the post as advertising given who published it.
